publications.title: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts
publications.summary: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts 22 October 2026 Market Abuse MiFID - Secondary Markets Short Selling Simplification and Burden Reduction The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU regulator and supervisor, has updated its Questions and Answers (Q&As) on market structure under MiFID II , the Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and the Short Selling Regulation (SSR) , removing outdated, duplicative and no longer relevant guidance as part of its Simplification and Burden Reduction (SBR) initiative . The exercise focused on identifying Q&As that are no longer relevant due to legislative amendments that are reflected in established market practices, or that are covered by other ESMA guidance. publications.title: FCA calls on private market firms to manage conflicts of interest in line with rapid growth
publications.summary: Private market firms vary in how well they identify and manage conflicts of interest, according to an FCA review. Private markets refer to investments in assets, companies, or debt not listed or traded on public exchanges. They’ve grown significantly in recent years, and the UK is a leading international centre. Private markets play an increasingly important role in providing capital to businesses and opportunities for returns to investors. Private markets can give rise to conflicts that differ from those in public markets, and effective disclosure is important to enable investors to assess whether their interests are being protected.The FCA found examples of good practice by firms across private equity, private credit and real estate asset classes. publications.title: FCA restricts 6 firms following concerns over anti-money laundering controls
publications.summary: Restrictions have been placed on 6 unregulated lenders, known as Annex 1 firms, after the FCA raised concerns about their anti-money laundering policies, controls and procedures while assessing their applications. The restrictions were imposed by the FCA on each firm’s request and limit their ability to take on new customers or do new business with existing customers, including extending existing credit.This action forms part of the FCA’s enhanced oversight of Annex 1 firms. These firms operate in sectors that can present a heightened risk of money laundering and other financial crime and are required to register with the FCA for supervision under the Money Laundering Regulations. They are not authorised or subject to wider FCA regulation.The FCA has previously warned Annex 1 firms that they will be subject to increased scrutiny. publications.title: News shocks and inflation: theory and evidence from large oil discoveries
publications.summary: We study hownews shocks affect inflation in open economies, using large oil and gas discoveries with realized production lags of at least five years as observable news about future output. Panel local projections show that discoveries raise core consumer prices over the subsequent decade, with about half the increase occurring prior to extraction.
